full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha J: In this appeal leave was granted to consider the questions as to whether this Division has committed any error apparent on the face of the judgment in CP No. 1075 of 2003 in maintaining the judgment of the High Court Division which has affirmed the decree for compensation at the rate of Taka 5,000 per day from the date of termination of the tenancy by legal notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act while passing a decree for ejectment and secondly, whether in the absence of sufficient pleadings, prayer, evidence and findings in support of compensation, the court has power to pass such decree. 

 2. Facts are shortly narrated as under. Respondents instituted a regular suit in the Civil Court for ejectment of the appellant from the suit premises on the ground of default in paying monthly rents. Appellant, a school, contested the suit claiming that it was not a defaulter the monthly rents were being deposited regularly in a rent control suit on their refusal to accept the same. The trial Court observed that the appellant was a defaulter; that the period of lease in respect of the suit premises expired on 10th March, 2001 and accordingly, decreed the suit. While passing the decree, it also directed that— 

 3. The above direction suggested that while passing the decree for ejectment, it also decreed compensation but the amount of compensation had not been specified and stated that the amount would be calculated and recovered on the basis of the respondents' claim, if not paid in the meantime. The trial Court did not make any finding on the point of sustaining any loss or damage by the respondents due to the appellant's remaining in possession as tenant in the premises. In the operating part of the judgment, it was directed that the appellant shall vacate the premises within 25th November, 2002, failing which, it was further directed that the respondents would be entitled to possession through the process of the court. The High Court Division maintained the decree in its entirety. Appellant then moved a leave petition in this Division which also affirmed the judgment of the High Court Division. 

 4. Admittedly no prayer was made in the plaint seeking a decree for awarding compensation. Even no foundation was laid in the plaint on the point of claiming compensation. Naturally, no issue was framed on the point of compensation and no finding was also made by the trial Court. In the legal notice, Ext-7, issued on behalf of the respondents determining the tenancy, it was pointed out that 'you are requested to deliver the vacant possession of the premises on 1-2-1999 to my client(s) or their representatives failing which legal action would be taken against you and you would be charged a sum of Taka 5,000 per diem by your illegal occupation of the tenanted premises'. On a cursory glance of the trial Court's judgment it may be presumed that it passed the decree on the assumption that since the appellant did not vacate the premises as per demand of the respondents in their legal notice and since the period of tenancy expired, the respondents are entitled to compensation on the basis of their claim made in the legal notice. 

 5. In the High Court Division it was argued on behalf of the appellant that the direction given on the question of compensation was beyond the power of the Court. The High Court Division did not address the point and maintained the decree observing: 'the trial Court committed no illegality in decreeing the suit and the impugned judgment and decree do not call for any interference by this Court'. In course of hearing of the leave petition, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant submitted that the appellant agitated in the High Court Division that it was not liable to pay damage of Taka 5,000 per day for staying in the suit premises even after expiry of lease the learned Judges of the High Court Division seriously erred in law in not deciding the point though noticed in the judgment... In course of the hearing of the leave petition as well, it was urged that 'the petitioner (appellant) is not liable to pay damage of Taka 5,000 a day for staying in the premises even after expiry of the lease....' and thus, a serious injustice has been caused to the petitioner'. This Division did not deal with the point and affirmed the judgment of the High Court Division. 

 6. It was urged on behalf of the appellant that in the absence of pleadings, prayer, evidence and findings on the question of compensation, this Division has committed error of law in maintaining the judgment of the High Court Division so far as it relates to the decree for compensation. Learned counsel appearing for the respondents finds it difficult to repel the contention and argues that the trial Court, in fact has not passed any decree for compensation and that the respondents are also not claiming any such compensation. 

 7. This admission of the learned counsel is sufficient to dispose of the appeal but the operating part of the judgment as quoted above shows otherwise. Moreso, the materials on record reveal that the respondents are really and in fact claiming compensation on the basis of the direction given in the operating part of the judgment of the trial Court and the trial Court has drawn up decree accordingly. The appellant has enclosed the copy of the decree drawn up by the trial Court on 7th October, 2002 by filing an additional paper book wherein the trial Court reproduced the words used in the operating part of the decree in verbatim. Naturally, if this decree on the question of compensation remains, there would arise various complications if the respondents proceed, with the execution proceeding. There is, therefore, need for examining the point in controversy despite the submission of the learned counsel for the respondents. 

 8. In the judgment, the High Court Division observed that after the dismissal of Rent  Case No. 15 of 1998, the appellant did not pay rent; that he is therefore, not entitled to get any protection from being evicted as a tenant and that the lease agreement having expired after March, 2001, the appellant was no longer a tenant under the respondents. This Division has reproduced the above observations of the High Court Division and dismissed the petition without meeting the point argued. Therefore, we find substance in the contention of the learned counsel that the High Court Division as well as this Division protanto affirmed the decree for compensation as claimed by the respondents in their legal notice. Now the question that calls for consideration is under what circumstances can a Court pass decree or order, for awarding compensation to a party to the suit. In this connection section 95 of the Code of Civil Procedure is relevant for resolving the point in dispute, which reads: 

 15. Therefore, there is apparent error in the judgment of this Division in maintaining the decree for compensation. The impugned judgment so far as it relates to maintaining the decree for compensation is required to be reviewed. The words- 

 16. Wherever appear in the judgment and the decree are hereby expunged.
